executivePulse.interpretation: The situation in memory and AI infrastructure remains strained. Enterprise SSD, Server DRAM / RDIMM, HBM are currently among the most constrained areas. The Daily Check from 2026-08-18 reviewed 8 current relevant reports; there is no confirmed material directional change at present. New capacity and improved yields could relieve pressure but will reach the market with a delay. For buyers, supply assurance, alternative BOMs and early procurement remain critical.

signals.title: Liquid Cooling Becomes Standard for High-End AI Infrastructure, with Penetration Expected to Reach 53% in 2026, Says TrendForce
signals.summary: Liquid cooling penetration among AI chips is projected to rise to 53% in 2026 and approach 60% in 2027. High-end chips from NVIDIA, AMD, and Google are driving the adoption of liquid cooling. NVIDIA’s rack-scale solution shipments are expected to double in 2026, while more than 80% of Google’s AI servers already use liquid cooling.
signals.analysis: This report is relevant for datacentre storage: it can affect prices, available capacities and procurement strategies for enterprise SSDs. Increased adoption of liquid cooling can shift server designs and BOMs, with potential lead times before storage supply adjusts.

signals.title: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.summary: Aktuelle Meldung von Reuters: Nvidia to provide up to $105 billion guarantee for OpenAI's Ohio data center
signals.analysis: The report alters the build-out trajectory for AI and datacentre infrastructure. Greater productive compute capacity will pull demand for server memory, enterprise storage, networking and power provisioning.
